result.topic_en: Problem II reduces Lagrange's general divisor form frr+grs+hss with 4fh−gg=n to an equivalent form whose middle coefficient is smaller than both outer coefficients, and two corollaries show that this bounds g by √(n/3), leaving only finitely many forms to check.

Problema II.

§. 6. Formam generalem diuisorum ante inuentam,
$frr+grs+hss$, in qua sit $4fh-gg=n$, in aliam eius-
dem formae, $f'tt+g'tu+h'uu$, transmutare, in qua sit
$g'<f'$ vel $h'$; manente proprietate $4f'h'-g'g'=n$.

Solutio.

Ponamus esse $f<h$ et numerum $g$ quantumuis esse
maiorem quam $f$, ac statuamus $r=t-\alpha s$, quo valore sub-
stituto orietur ista forma:
$$ftt+(g-2\alpha f)ts+(\alpha\alpha f-\alpha g+h)ss;$$
vbi manifesto $\alpha$ ita assumi poterit, vt fiat $g-2\alpha f<f$,
vbi quidem animaduertendum est, nihil referre, verum
$g-2\alpha f$ prodeat positiuum an negatiuum. Statuatur igi-
tur $g-2\alpha f=\pm g'$, ita vt certe sit $g'<f'$, cum vero ob
analogiam loco $f$ scribatur $f'$ et $\alpha\alpha f-\alpha g+h=h'$ eritque
$$4f'h'-g'g'=4fh-gg=n.$$
Hoc igitur modo forma proposita reducta est ad hanc:
$$f'tt\pm g'ts+h'ss,$$

Corollarium 1.

§. 7. Hoc igitur modo infinita multitudo formula-
rum $frr+grs+hss$, in qua $4fh-gg=n$ ple-
rumque ad satis exiguum numerum reduci potest, dum sci-

ficiens medius $g$ maior est alterutro extremorum.

Corollarium 2.

§. 8. Cum igitur sit tam $f>g$ quam $h>g$, erit
$4fh>4gg$. Sit igitur $4fh=4gg+\Delta$, et cum esse
debeat $4fh-gg=\pm n$ [?], erit $3gg+\Delta=\pm n$ [?], ideoque
$3gg<\pm n$ [?], hinc ergo $g<\sqrt{\frac{\pm n}{3}}$; quamobrem loco $g$ suc-
cessiue eos tantum valores assumsisse sufficiet, qui sunt mi-
nores quam $\sqrt{\frac{\pm n}{3}}$, ex quibus singulis facile colligentur va-
lores litterarum $f$ et $h$ ex aequatione $4fh=gg+n$,
quo facto omnes plane diuisores formae $pp+nqq$ certe
continebuntur in quapiam harum formularum simpliciorum.

items.quote: Praecipuum igitur inuentum, quod Illustri la Grange acceptum referre debemus, in hoc consistit, quod infinitam illam huiusmodi formularum multitudinem ad exiguum numerum pro quouis casu reuocare docuit
items.english: The principal discovery, which we owe to the illustrious Lagrange, consists in this: he taught how to reduce that infinite multitude of such formulas to a small number in every case.

items.quote: Formam generalem diuisorum ante inuentam, $frr+grs+hss$, in qua sit $4fh-gg=n$, in aliam eiusdem formae, $f'tt+g'tu+h'uu$, transmutare, in qua sit $g'<f'$ vel $h'$; manente proprietate $4f'h'-g'g'=n$.
items.english: To transform the general form of divisors found earlier, frr+grs+hss with 4fh−gg=n, into another of the same form f'tt+g'tu+h'uu in which g' is less than f' or h', while keeping the property 4f'h'−g'g'=n.

items.quote: Hoc igitur modo infinita multitudo formularum $frr+grs+hss$, in qua $4fh-gg=n$ plerumque ad satis exiguum numerum reduci potest, dum scilicet omnes illae formulae excludi possunt, in quibus coëfficiens medius $g$ maior est alterutro extremorum.
items.english: In this way the infinite multitude of formulas frr+grs+hss with 4fh−gg=n can usually be reduced to a fairly small number, since all formulas whose middle coefficient g exceeds either of the outer coefficients can be excluded.

items.quote: quamobrem loco $g$ successiue eos tantum valores assumsisse sufficiet, qui sunt minores quam $\sqrt{\frac{\pm n}{3}}$, ex quibus singulis facile colligentur valores litterarum $f$ et $h$ ex aequatione $4fh=gg+n$, quo facto omnes plane diuisores formae $pp+nqq$ certe continebuntur in quapiam harum formularum simpliciorum.
items.english: Therefore it will suffice to take for g successively only values smaller than √(±n/3). From each of these the values of f and h are easily obtained from the equation 4fh=gg+n, and then all divisors of the form pp+nqq will certainly be contained in one of these simpler formulas.
